summary.motive: Get two blockers on the perimeter before the ball carrier arrives, collapsing contain inward so the sweep can turn upfield.
summary.whyItWorks: The double pull attacks the edge with sequential kick-out and lead blocks, and the wing's arc removes the last force player exactly as the ball turns the corner.
summary.failureMode: The end spills the kick-out and funnels the sweep inside, or the force safety squeezes the arc instead of taking the kick.

beats.title: 1. The Double Pull
beats.text: Both guards pull in opposite roles: the playside guard kicks flat toward the end while the backside guard pulls as the lead through the hole. The entire defense's eyes snap to the backfield.

beats.title: 2. Kick-Out and Deep Handoff
beats.text: The quarterback reverse-pivots and extends the handoff to B at depth while the guard logs the end inside. The sweep lane is now two gaps wide.

beats.title: 3. The Perimeter Block Sequence
beats.text: The wing kicks the force corner out just as the pulling guard arrives on the linebacker. Every defender who could squeeze the edge is being blocked outward.

beats.title: 4. Turn Upfield Behind Escorts
beats.text: With containment collapsed inward and force displaced, B turns north at the numbers with escorts leading him into the open grass.

relations.tell: Both guards leave their gaps at the same instant — no other Wing-T series moves both interior linemen horizontally on the snap.
